items.context: UM-SCC-11B and UM-SCC-81B laryngeal carcinoma lines (p53 mutant with loss of heterozygosity), 6 Gy gamma, with or without nutlin-3 5 uM

perturbation.approximation: p53 mutation with LOH treated as loss of function

claims.statement: No detectable senescence (SA-beta-gal) under any condition.
claims.quote: Cells expressing full-length mutant p53 with LOH (UM-SCC-11B and UM-SCC-81B, the most radiosensitive) did not show any detectable senescence under any of the conditions examined.

items.context: UM-SCC-17A and UM-SCC-17AS (p53 wild type), nutlin-3 alone, no irradiation

perturbation.approximation: nutlin-3 blocks the MDM2-p53 interaction; modelled as Mdm2 loss

claims.statement: Increased G1 and decreased S phase.
claims.quote: Figure 3 summarises the results (also see Supplementary Data Figure 2) from a typical experiment, and shows that there is a reduction in the S-phase population and a concomitant increase in the G1 population in the wild-type cells with increasing doses of Nutlin-3.

claims.statement: No increase in sub-G1; absent here means not induced.
claims.quote: As shown in Figure 3, flow cytometry did not detect any increase in the sub-G1 population of cells in response to Nutlin-3 treatment, and thus we conclude that this is unlikely to provide an explanation for this effect.

items.context: HCT116 p53-/-, 5 Gy gamma, apoptosis measured as sub-G0 DNA content over time

claims.statement: Significant time-dependent increase (P<0.05); the paper reports no difference in apoptotic ratio from p53+/+.
claims.quote: Following treatment with 5 Gy γ-irradiation, the average apoptotic percentages of cell number significantly increased in a time-dependent manner in the p53+/+ and p53−/− cells (P<0.05), whereas there was no change in the apoptotic cell number in the non-irradiated control cells (Fig. 1A).

items.context: HCT116 p53-/-, 5 Gy gamma, cell cycle at 24 and 48 h

claims.statement: Cells that left G1 accumulated in G2 at 48 h, whereas p53+/+ cells arrested in S.
claims.quote: Following treatment with irradiation, G1/S cell cycle arrest occurred in the p53+/+ cells, whereas the p53−/− cells accumulated in the G2 phase.

items.context: MK-1775 (WEE1 inhibitor) 200 nM with irradiation; p53-defective H1299, Calu-6, MDA-MB-231, PC3 versus p53 wild-type A549, H460, MCF-7, LnCap, CCD-16, MCF-10A. Replicated for H1299, FaDu, Calu-6 and A549 in bridges2016 Table 1.

claims.statement: Not radiosensitised, factor about 1.0.
claims.quote: Tumor cells with wild-type p53 and cells of normal tissue origin were not similarly radiosensitized.

claims.statement: The radiation-induced G2 block was abrogated.

claims.statement: No abrogation.
claims.quote: Consistent with its ability to radiosensitize, MK-1775 abrogated the radiation-induced G2 block in p53-defective cells but not in p53 wild-type lines.

claims.statement: Retaining one wild-type copy does not make cells more radiosensitive to pre-treatment with Nutlin-3.
claims.quote: Not only does retention of one wild-type copy in the presence of a mutant p53 allele (heterozygous mutation) not render cells sensitive to the growth inhibitory effects of Nutlin-3 (Figure 1) but it also does not render the cells more radiosensitive (Figure 4).

items.context: mouse intestinal crypts, conditional c-Myc deletion (AhCre Myc fl/fl) versus wild type, 14 Gy gamma irradiation, apoptosis 6 h later

perturbation.approximation: conditional gene deletion treated as loss of function; mouse tissue, not a cell line

claims.statement: The immediate wave of apoptosis after ionizing irradiation was completely abrogated (the figure shows a significant, not total, reduction; 'completely' is the authors' wording).
claims.quote: Remarkably, c-Myc deletion completely abrogated the immediate wave of apoptosis following both ionizing irradiation and cisplatin treatment, recapitulating the phenotype of p53 deficiency in the intestine.
